title: Lead Holdfast: weekly sync notes (Nov 18 2026)

body:
Purpose and framing:
This doc captures the Holdfast weekly cross-leads sync on 2026-11-18. The tone is operational: rapid surface of new technical regressions, short term mitigations, and alignment on customer-facing actions (billing/communications). We prioritized items that could impact SLAs or billing anomalies.

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick wins + incidents (5m)
2) Canary findings: batching v2 and KV-cache signals (8m)
3) Dedicated autoscale jitter and mitigations (6m)
4) Billing spike attribution + console telemetry (6m)
5) Action items, owners, next sync (5m)

Summary highlights:
- Canary for batching optimization v2 surfaced an unexpected KV-cache behavior: certain long-prefix requests that previously benefited from prefix cache now see slightly increased tail latency (~3% p99 uplift). This is reproducible in canary traffic subset (10k requests/hour). The immediate risk is user-visible tail spikes for some customers; we've paused full rollout.
- Dedicated capacity autoscaler shows high-frequency oscillation in us-west-2 when combined with new instance replacement heuristics; we observed transient OOM events in a specific node class under burst traffic. Short-term damping proposed.
- A billing spike for a small set of enterprise customers last weekend remains partially unexplained: token counts are higher but route->customer attribution in console is incomplete for some legacy routes. Finance requested temporary telemetry to reconcile.
- Private deployment test infra does not yet exercise the latest HSM key rotation flows; one enterprise customer expects a cert rotation drill next week. This is a potential go/no-go for the private rollout schedule.

Detailed notes by agenda item:
1) Quick wins + incidents
- SRE reported two non-critical P1s closed: cache eviction storm in eu-central (hot keys) resolved by emergency config change; ownership: Noah.
- Small memory leak in the monitoring agent (observability repo) was committed; will land in edge channel this week.

2) Canary: batching v2 / KV-cache 
- Arjun presented the canary graphs: aggregate QPS and average latency improved, but kv-cache hit rate dropped for requests with long prompt prefixes (examples: docs ingestion pipelines and customer A's internal bot workload).
- Hypothesis: batching v2 altered tokenization boundary alignment or key composition for prefix keys, increasing cache fragmentation.
- Temporary mitigation: revert v2 in canary and roll partial instrumentation to capture full KV key fingerprints for a sampled 0.5% traffic.
- Decision: rollback canary v2 for now; run an expanded regression test with synthetic long-prefix traces.

3) Dedicated autoscale jitter
- Observed phenomenon: autoscaler scales nodes up and then down multiple times over short windows during burst; node churn leads to pod placement thrash and occasional OOM.
- Root-cause leads (Jenn + Liam) suspect interaction between replacement threshold (age-based) and burst scaling.
- Short-term fix: introduce autoscale damping and increase min-stable window from 30s to 3m for affected pools. Also add CPU headroom reserve policy for volatile pools.
- Long-term: revisit replacement heuristics and smoothing algorithm; proposal due next planning sync.

4) Billing spike attribution + console telemetry
- Finance flagged route-level spikes for 3 customers: needs mapping to customer IDs to reconcile invoices. Console currently aggregates some legacy routes under generic ids.
- Evelyn to push a feature-flagged console endpoint to expose route->customer mapping and enable fine-grained telemetry for one week for reconciliation. Sampling at 0.1% to start.
- We agreed to hold outward-facing billing notes until reconciliation completes to avoid unnecessary churn.

5) Private deployment HSM tests
- Liam called out missing HSM rotation coverage in the private test harness. A customer-facing rotation drill is scheduled; if we cannot demonstrate the flow, it will delay the private deployment acceptance.
- Action: add HSM rotation job to the nightly private test matrix and validate key rotation end-to-end by 2026-11-24.

Communications and customer impact
- No broad customer communication required yet. For the customers showing billing anomalies, finance will prepare private reconciliations once we expose mapping.
- For customers on the v2 canary cohort, CS will send a short note that we are pausing and investigating — we will not characterize as a regression until we finish tests.

Risks and mitigation priorities (short list)
- Risk: tail latency regressions propagate to SLA violations for a small group of customers. Mitigation: rollback canary, expanded regression tests, and additional kv-cache telemetry.
- Risk: node churn in Dedicated leads to reduced capacity during peak. Mitigation: enable damping, increase min-stable window, soak 48h.
- Risk: private customer acceptance delayed by HSM gap. Mitigation: add rotation test to nightly and escalate support resources if needed.

Open questions / Discussion items for follow-up:
- Do we need broader KV-cache key-format invariants enforced at runtime to prevent future fragmentation? (engineering-design session suggested).
- Is 0.1% telemetry sampling sufficient for finance reconciliation, or do we need higher sampling for a narrow time window? Finance to advise.
- Should we formalize a short ‘holdfast’ runbook for rapid cross-team rollback coordination (roles, comms, escalation)? Maya proposed drafting a one-page runbook.

Next steps and cadence
- Immediate: rollback canary + set up instrumentation (Arjun, Jenn) by 2026-11-19 EOD.
- Autoscale damping soak (Noah + Liam) run 2026-11-19 through 2026-11-21; interim report 2026-11-20.
- Console mapping patch to finance (Evelyn) by 2026-11-20.
- Follow-up holdfast quick sync: 2026-11-19 09:30 PT (30m).

- Canary dashboard: runtime/canary/v2/nov18

summary: Operational weekly cross-leads capture: rollback canary for batching v2 due to KV-cache tail latency regression, autoscale damping for Dedicated pools to address jitter/ooms, add console telemetry for billing reconciliation, add HSM rotation tests for private deployments. Follow-up sync scheduled 2026-11-19.
